# Out-of-Bounds / Invalid Coordinates

A point with latitude exceeding the valid range (100° instead of max 90°). This typically indicates a lat/lon coordinate swap or data entry error. GeoJSON requires [Longitude, Latitude] order, but many systems use [Lat, Lon].

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Case ID | `out_of_bounds_coordinates` |
| Category | vector |
| Format | GeoJSON |
| Geometry type | Point |
| CRS | `EPSG:4326` |
| Test tier | unit |
| Size class | tiny |
| Storage class | bundled |
| Redistributable | yes |
| Loader | `geopandas` |
| Status | validated |

## Use this case

```python
import pytest


@pytest.mark.geocase_case("out_of_bounds_coordinates")
def test_out_of_bounds_coordinates(geocase_case) -> None:
    data = geocase_case.load()
    assert data is not None
```

## What this case checks

Expose code that silently accepts coordinates outside valid geographic ranges. Latitude must be in [-90, 90], longitude in [-180, 180]. Values exceeding these ranges indicate data errors or coordinate order swaps.
